entries.summary: Check, list, get and search the contract data files (connections, role assignments, data policy, capabilities, features, versions, settings, extensions)
entries.inputs: a data id, an entry id or search words
entries.outputs: JSON or text; exit 1 with a catalog code when a file is invalid or an id is unknown

entries.summary: Write a candidate of one data file with global_id and install_id added to every record that lacks them, nothing else changed; apply it with stella-apply.py
entries.inputs: an index row id (<id>/<file>.json for a folder row) and --out <new file>
entries.outputs: the candidate file; exit 1 with a catalog code: STL-CFG-311 when the row is unknown, STL-CFG-313 when --out lies inside a stack tree (the root, the tree the tool runs from, any folder holding an index), STL-CFG-310 when the file cannot be written

entries.summary: List the field paths each schema marks x-owner-only (only the owner's path writes them)
entries.outputs: schema and JSON pointer per line, or {schema: [paths]}; exit 1 with STL-CFG-310 when a schema cannot be read

entries.summary: Lint the test map and select the selftests a change can affect
entries.outputs: selftest names, or full

entries.summary: Render, explain and validate alert codes; regenerate docs/alert-codes.md
entries.outputs: the plain alert text

entries.summary: What a role needs from any model that serves it: tool calling, context size, vision and the data classes it may see
entries.outputs: JSON; exit 1 with STL-CFG-311 when the role is unknown

entries.summary: Count literal provider, model, host, board, project and channel names in code against the baseline
entries.outputs: exit 0 clean, 1 over the baseline, 2 with STL-CFG-310 when an input cannot be read

entries.summary: Append one chained line to the trusted event log with secrets masked (owner tools only), read its last lines, or verify its chain
entries.inputs: an event (who, what, old, new), a line count, or verify [--json]
entries.outputs: one JSON line per event (schema_version 3: writer, seq, prev, mac); verify: the problems with their line numbers (STL-EVT-901..906) and the legacy count; STL-CFG-318 when the log cannot be written, STL-CFG-312 in a worker environment

entries.summary: Report drift of an applied data file and list its apply history
entries.outputs: drift lines or history; STL-CFG-314 on drift

entries.summary: Apply or roll back a data file through the apply contract: dry run, backup, idempotent apply, one event line
entries.inputs: a data file id and a candidate file; for an owner-only file optionally a proof file (--proof) instead of the host's owner key
entries.outputs: the change summary (a dry run of an owner-only file also prints the action a proof must cover); STL-CFG-312 for a worker on an owner-only file, STL-OWN-801..813 without a valid owner proof (806 no owner key, 808 an identity-critical change without its typed phrase), STL-CFG-313 when the candidate is invalid

entries.summary: The owner's command to read or change one setting from the settings registry: validates the value, then writes through the apply contract
entries.inputs: a setting key and, to change it, a value; optionally a proof file (--proof) instead of the host's owner key
entries.outputs: the value or the change summary; STL-CFG-311 for an unknown key, STL-CFG-312 for a worker, STL-CFG-313 for a store file that holds a key twice, STL-CFG-315 for a bad value, STL-OWN-806 without an owner key, STL-OWN-808 when an identity-critical setting is changed without its typed phrase

entries.summary: Which paths are owner settings and owner data, and which files define the owner boundary (a card that changes one needs the owner to say so at the merge)
entries.outputs: a JSON list of paths; exit 1 when the role table or the data index cannot be read

entries.summary: The owner-authenticator: check the owner-auth policy, list its providers, create the owner key (setup), make and verify owner proofs bound to one exact action, a nonce and an expiry
entries.inputs: an action file {op, target, old_digest, new_digest | new}, an action class and, to verify, a proof file
entries.outputs: a proof (JSON) or the provider ids used; STL-CFG-312 in a worker environment, STL-CFG-310 for an invalid policy, STL-OWN-801..809 and 811..813 for a refused proof or key; an accepted device-signed request writes one remote alert (policy remote.alert_code)

entries.summary: List the stubs (features entries with due_phase and replaced_by) due at or before a phase of the features phase order; fails while one is due
entries.inputs: a phase of the features phase_order
entries.outputs: JSON or text: the stubs due {id, due_phase, replaced_by}; exit 1 with STL-OWN-810 when any is due, 2 for an unknown phase

entries.summary: Append one line marked untrusted to the agents' event stream (never proof of anything)
entries.outputs: one JSON line with "trusted": false in the untrusted stream; STL-CFG-313 for an invalid or oversized line, STL-CFG-318 when the stream cannot be written

entries.summary: The approval service (host side): make approval requests bound to an exact action, a nonce and an expiry, take agents' approval-ask lines in, deliver requests on the channel adapters, collect and decide answers (owner proof per channel kind), and tell a request's status from the trusted event log
entries.inputs: an action file and class, summary, card and ttl; a request id; a channel id; a decision (approved or denied)
entries.outputs: the request record (JSON), a message ref, decided answers, or pending/approved/denied/expired; STL-CFG-312 in a worker environment, STL-OWN-820..831 for a refused answer, request or adapter

entries.summary: List the paired devices of the device registry, or check it (schema, each id once, Ed25519 public keys); pairing and revoking are owner writes of the devices row through apply
entries.outputs: the entries (JSON array with --json), or check's verdict; exit 1 with STL-CFG-310 when the registry is invalid

entries.summary: Test double of the primary lease: claim, release or show the one lease per account in a state file (U1 builds the real lease)
entries.inputs: claim|release|show with --state FILE --account A [--engine E] [--ttl S]
entries.outputs: the lease (JSON, the primary-lease contract) or null; STL-OWN-814 when another engine holds it or a non-holder releases

entries.summary: Judge a request to the local HTTP API against the loopback API contract: Host, Origin (every request), endpoint, API token, Origin and CSRF token on a state-changing request, owner proof on an owner-write endpoint (the library the real API calls; the CLI replays one request)
entries.inputs: a request file {method, path, headers, body, session {api_token, csrf_token, port}}
entries.outputs: {ok, code[, cause, message]} on stdout; exit 0 allowed, 1 refused with STL-OWN-850..858 and one alert line; an accepted owner proof is spent

entries.summary: The loopback API's test double: serves the contract's endpoints on the IPv4 loopback address and a free port with the loopback guard in front, and does nothing else (until E1 builds the real API)
entries.inputs: --port P (0 = a free port) and --session F ({api_token, csrf_token})
entries.outputs: the bound port on the first stdout line; HTTP 200 {ok: true} or 4xx {ok: false, code[, cause], message} per request; STL-OWN-858/859 when it cannot start

entries.summary: The ordered chain of model links a role may use right now, and why (presets, data policy, grants, card facts, health)
entries.inputs: a role, a project, optionally a card, task tier, driver and task id, and a rung N of the role's escalation chain (--rung; host-side callers only, refused in a worker environment)
entries.outputs: JSON; exit 1 with a catalog code when no link is usable, a card app is refused or an id is unknown; every chain entry carries its effort; with --rung N >= 1: rung {requested, served, last, link, skipped[]}, STL-MDL-731 when no rung is left (escalate to the owner), and the CLI writes one trusted event line per skipped rung (STL-MDL-732) and one when the walk is exhausted

entries.summary: Model call and failover along the resolver's chain: call (the engine loop), attempt (one link for a worker CLI's launcher) and result (how the attempt ended); cooldown, loop guard, mid-task checks, less-private notice, one trusted event line per pick and switch
entries.inputs: call|attempt --role R --project P [--card C] [--tier T] [--driver D] --task ID --json (call: prompt on stdin; [--rung N]: the chain is the resolver's rung N walk, bin/escalate.sh's call); result --task ID --link <connection>/<model> --outcome ok|<trigger id>
entries.outputs: JSON {task, link, link_class, text, tool_calls, usage, model, switches, failure_history, refused, stubs}; exit 1 with a catalog code; exit 3 when a link needs a grant

entries.summary: Capability probe of a model link (host only): tries the link through its wire shape and records tool calling, parallel tool calls, JSON, the strongest output shape it proves, family and effective context per model version in the probe records (protected state, index key probe_records); one probe.recorded event line per record; due lists the links whose model version has no record; check judges the file.
entries.inputs: run --connection C --model M [--again] --json | due --json | show [--connection C] [--model M] --json | check --json
entries.outputs: JSON (run: the record; due: {due, unreachable}; show: {records, problem}; check: {ok, records, problem}); exit 1 with a catalog code (STL-MDL-734 unknown link, 735 version already probed, 736 no usable answer, STL-CFG-312 in a worker environment)

entries.summary: Triage router (host only): a small local model, called through route.py for the router role, classifies one input (stdin) into a route of the routing data's triage tiers (or the image route when the input carries an image); confidence is the route label's token probability where the link gives it, else the agreement of triage.samples calls; unsure or below the threshold moves one tier up, never down; inside a project a message is work unless it is a confident pure question; one triage.verdict event line per verdict (its id); label records an owner override or reroute (triage.label); fit sets the threshold from the labelled verdicts (triage calibration state, triage.calibrated); an optional classifier behind the features.json flag triage-classifier (off by default).
entries.inputs: route [--project P] [--image] --json (message on stdin) | label --id ID --route R --source override|reroute --json | fit --json
entries.outputs: JSON (route: {id, route, confidence, unsure, tier_moved, link, reasoning?}; label: {id, route, source, label_id}; fit: {threshold, labels}); exit 1 with a catalog code (STL-MDL-740 no verdict could be made, 741 label refused, 742 calibration refused, STL-CFG-312 in a worker environment)

entries.summary: Build team preset (host only): generate writes the Claude Code agent files (the folder of the data index key agents_dir) of every agent of the team preset (index key team_preset; role-assignments effort_modes agents: description, tools, link, fallbacks, escalation_chain) with the body texts of the folder team_bodies and a generated marker, one team.generated event line; check compares the preset, the files and the models the latest session log shows (a hand edit, a stale file, an agent on a model its preset does not list fail; an agent with no transcript is not seen; a file without the marker is unmanaged), one alert line on failure.
entries.inputs: generate [--preset ID] [--out DIR] --json | check [--preset ID] [--sessions DIR] --json
entries.outputs: JSON (generate: {preset, written}; check: {preset, ok, latest_session, agents[{agent, ok, session, problems}], stale, unmanaged}); exit 1 with a catalog code (STL-MDL-743 cannot generate or check, 744 a file differs or is stale, 745 an agent ran on a model its preset does not list)

entries.summary: Routing consent: the accept popup for a link that needs a grant, project-scoped grants applied through the apply tool, unattended queue; pending, complete, revoke
entries.outputs: JSON; exit 1 with a catalog code

entries.summary: The one interface for keys until the secrets broker: reports the state of the key backend the routing data names; a value is returned in-process to the model call only and never printed
entries.outputs: {backend, kind, ok, missing}; exit 0 when the backend holds every name, else 1 with a catalog code; never a value

entries.summary: The effective settings of a project: each value, the active preset, Local only, each role's class order, pins and fallbacks, the grants in force, and whether each is inherited or overridden
entries.outputs: JSON or a plain table; exit 1 with a catalog code when the data is invalid

entries.summary: Test rig: a local mock model server serving every wire shape of the protocols data, with faults on demand and an exact call counter
entries.inputs: optional STELLA_ROOT; faults set by a POST to the control URL
entries.outputs: first stdout line {port, control}; GET /_calls returns counts and the requests seen

entries.summary: Test rig: a fake coding CLI standing in for a cli-login connection; reports a usage limit, a timeout or a missing model on request
entries.inputs: a prompt on stdin; MOCK_CLI_MODE, MOCK_CLI_SECONDS, MOCK_CLI_CALLS, MOCK_CLI_USAGE (a plan-share usage block on stderr)
entries.outputs: a result JSON, or a non-zero exit with a message; a calls file with argv and env names

entries.summary: Sound comparison of two arms on the same tasks (paired trials, mean difference with a 95% t-interval, pass^k, non-inferiority margin, minimum sample, regression set) and routing stats from benchmark results (benchmark mean over the advertised score only above the minimum sample); record adds benchmark records with their trusted event lines (host only). Parameters are data in .stella/model-check.json.
entries.inputs: compare --a FILE --b FILE [--cheaper] [--regression FILE] --json | stats [--prior FILE] --json | record --file FILE --json | check --json
entries.outputs: JSON (compare: {decision better|worse|non_inferior|inconclusive, reason, n_tasks, mean_diff, ci, pass_k}; stats: a list of {role, connection, model, score, source, n, reason}; record: {recorded}; check: {ok, benchmark_records}); exit 1 with a catalog code (STL-MDL-750 bad input, 751 regression set failed, 752 parameters unusable, 753 benchmark results unusable, STL-CFG-312 record in a worker environment)

entries.summary: Usage ledger and limits (host only): appends one record per model call (connection, model, role, project, card, tokens, outcome; secrets scrubbed), counts the daily cap from the records of the UTC day, holds flock slots across every process (hold runs a command inside the slots and frees them when it ends or is killed), keeps limits observed from a 429, rate-limit headers or a CLI's limit error with their expiry (one trusted event line each), and reports status and usage per card, project, role, model or connection. Limits come from the catalog (a value or a limits.env key), the signals from .stella/limit-signals.json.
entries.inputs: record --json (call on stdin) | status --connection C [--model M] --json | hold --connection C --model M [--holder H] -- CMD... | observe --connection C [--model M] [--status N --header 'Name: v'] --json (answer body or CLI output on stdin) | report --by card|project|role|model|connection --json | check --json
entries.outputs: JSON (record: the record; status: {concurrency, daily, observed, plan_share, problems}; observe: the observed limit or null; report: {by, groups, torn}; check: {ok, records, torn, observed, problem}); hold becomes CMD, or exits 75 no free slot, 76 daily cap used, 77 observed limit active (STL-LIM-412); exit 1 with a catalog code (STL-LIM-410 unknown link, 411 record refused, 413 file or lock unusable, 414 check failed, 415 limit unreadable, STL-CFG-312 in a worker environment)

entries.summary: Cost accounting: prices a usage record from the dated pricing table (.stella/pricing.json; five token types priced apart, batch discount, a cli-login record has no cost and keeps its plan share, a model with no row is unpriced with one STL-LIM-420 alert), makes the OpenTelemetry GenAI span of a record (appended to the spans file, index key spans), rolls records up by card, project, role, model or connection with the cache-hit rate, judges the table (check), and exports spans as OTLP/HTTP JSON to the enabled otlp-export app of the connections catalog only while the features.json flag otlp-export is on (off by default; nothing is sent otherwise).
entries.inputs: price [--record FILE|-] --json | span [--record FILE|-] [--write] --json | rollup --by card|project|role|model|connection [--records FILE] --json | check --json | export [--record FILE|-|--spans] --json
entries.outputs: JSON (price: {cost, plan_share}; span: the span; rollup: {by, groups, skipped}; check: {ok, entries}; export: {exported, flag, reason?}); exit 1 with a catalog code (STL-LIM-421 table unusable, STL-LIM-422 export failed, STL-LIM-423 input unusable); STL-LIM-420 is an alert line, not a failure

entries.summary: Cost levers: the batch lane (only a listed job kind that is not urgent, on a connection that offers batch; an urgent job never), the cache policy per connection with the lifetime chosen from the measured gap between calls, the prefix lint of consecutive prompts (a changed stable part or volatile text fails), the cache-hit rate per role from the ledger; the library also lays prompts out stable-first with tools only added, and fans parallel reviewers out after the first call's first token (a test double of the scheduler M1). Every rule is in .stella/levers.json.
entries.inputs: lane --job FILE|- --json | policy --connection C [--records FILE] --json | lint-prefix PATH... --json | hitrate --by card|project|role|model|connection [--records FILE] --json | check --json
entries.outputs: JSON (lane: {lane, batch, reason}; policy: {kind, breakpoints, lifetime, gap_seconds, covered, source}; lint-prefix: {ok, compared}; hitrate: {by, groups, skipped}; check: {ok, entries}); exit 1 with a catalog code (STL-LIM-440 data unusable, 441 tool removed, 442 prefix lint failed, 443 fan-out stopped, 444 input unusable)

entries.summary: Budgets and cost anomalies: per project, card and role budgets from .stella/budgets.json (a * default per scope, a window, soft thresholds in percent, a hard cap in money and/or a plan-share cap) checked against the usage ledger; soft thresholds alert once each (STL-LIM-430); a hard cap makes one hold, one alert (431) and one approval request through bin/approvals.py, and every call of that key is refused (432) until an answer read from the trusted event log (approved: raise the cap or defer to a link the data policy allows; denied, expired or unanswered: paused); an estimate before a card starts and the actual with the difference at close; anomaly detectors (spend rate, retry loop, growing session, outlier card) with one alert (433) and one event line per episode; a before_call hook that bin/route.py call asks before any request (a hold refuses the call; an approved defer allows only its link and the budget stays measured).
entries.inputs: check [--project P] [--card C] [--role R] --json | hold list --json | estimate --kind K [--card C] --json | close --card C --json | anomalies --json | check-data --json
entries.outputs: JSON (check: {result allow|warn|held, threshold, defer_to, code, holds[]}; hold list: {holds}; estimate: {estimate, basis, samples}; close: {estimate, actual, difference}; anomalies: {new, known}; check-data: {ok, problems}); exit 1 with a catalog code (STL-LIM-432 held, 434 data or state unusable, 435 input unusable); 430, 431 and 433 are alert lines

entries.summary: The weekly model check (owner/engine command, host only): picks model links for preset roles from probe records, benchmark results with trusted lines and prices applied before the run, never from news, web text or model output; refuses any pick that widens exposure (link class, data policy, host, connection), lacks a probe record or ranks lower; applies each pick through the apply tool's engine exception (built-in presets while the owner setting MODEL_CHECK_BUILTIN is on, custom presets with a model_check grant), one event line and alert per pick, rollback from the trusted line, pricing refresh, pause and resume. Rules are data in .stella/model-check.json weekly.
entries.inputs: run [--dry-run] --json | status --json | rollback <pick id> --json | resume --json | check --json
entries.outputs: JSON (run: {picks, refused, skipped, ignored, failing, pricing}; status: {state, picks}; rollback: {rollback, pick}; resume: {resumed}; check: {ok, problems}); exit 1 with a catalog code (STL-MDL-761 pick not applied, 762 paused now, 763 paused, 764 the apply tool refused the engine pick, 765 rollback refused, STL-CFG-312 worker environment)

entries.summary: Prompt profiles: renders a role prompt in the form the model's family follows best (tag or heading sections, evidence first, capability line, working notes, question last, the family's parallel-tool-call line). Profile chosen by --profile, the role override, the catalog model's family, else the default; every form is in .stella/prompt-profiles.json.
entries.inputs: render --role R --link CONN/MODEL --brief FILE [--profile P] [--evidence FILE] [--attached FILE] [--notes FILE] [--instructions FILE] [--question FILE|TEXT] --json | check --json
entries.outputs: JSON (render: {profile, family, role, link, sections, reasoning, example_placement, parallel_tools, text}; check: {ok, entries}); exit 1 with a catalog code (STL-CFG-330 data unusable, 331 profile or link not found, 332 input unusable, 333 capability line missing)

entries.summary: Per-run tokens (host only): mint one for every run (api and cli-login; the record holds the connection type, DC-04) and print it once; revoke every token of a run. Only the sha256 of a token is stored (index key run_tokens); the prefix is data so leak scanners find one; one trusted event line per mint and revoke with a hash prefix, never the value
entries.inputs: mint --run R --role ROLE --card C --link <connection>/<model> [--project P] [--ttl S] | revoke --run R
entries.outputs: mint: the token alone on stdout; revoke: JSON {run, revoked}; exit 1 with a catalog code (STL-MDL-797 token state or gateway data, 799 link or ttl refused, STL-CFG-312 worker environment)

entries.summary: The loopback model proxy for api links (host only): takes a run token from the protocols' auth headers, refuses an unknown, expired, revoked or non-api token, pins the run's model, runs the budget gate and a ledger slot, swaps in the real key (credentials.get) with the protocol's header template, forwards only the protocol's paths to the connection's catalog host (no redirect, no environment proxy), streams the answer back with the key masked, records usage and cost, one event line per request
entries.inputs: serve [--port P]   (bind address, default port, body limit and passed headers from .stella/run-gateway.json)
entries.outputs: {bind, port, pid} on stdout and at the index key model_proxy_state; per request the upstream answer, or an HTTP status >= 400 with {error {code, message}} (STL-MDL-790..799, the budget's STL-LIM-43x); exit 1 with a catalog code when it cannot serve (STL-MDL-799, STL-CFG-312)

entries.summary: Find, describe, request and load capabilities by role: search ranks registry entries by id, keywords and summary (weights from .stella/capability-sources.json), a hidden id answers like an unknown one, request opens one approval through the approval service, load returns the definition and writes one trusted capability-load line (host side only); a skill or MCP server with no registry entry is hidden and raises an alert
entries.outputs: JSON or text; exit 1 with STL-GRD-660..667 when a capability is not known or not visible to the role

entries.summary: Decide a host-session or input-source request (host side, pure): the vault, the role's host_operator flag, an attended run, the owner present (indicator, kill switch, route, paired device with biometric), the owner's host access settings (master, routes, apps, domains, input sources, action states and reversible flags, overrides), request finality for irreversible actions and an approved confirmation for ask-first ones
entries.inputs: a request file {capability, role, run, target {app, domain}, action {type}, confirmation}
entries.outputs: allowed (exit 0, JSON with --json) or refused: exit 1 with STL-GRD-620..637, STL-CFG-312 in a worker environment

entries.summary: The capability MCP server on loopback (host only): MCP over streamable HTTP (JSON-RPC 2.0 POSTs) with the tools search, describe, request and load; the run token is the only credential and role, card and run come from its record (never from the arguments); Host and Origin must name a loopback host; it calls bin/capabilities.py in-process, so load and request write their trusted lines there; a worker's capabilities.py is its thin client
entries.inputs: serve [--port P]   (bind address, port, path, hosts, auth header, body limit, timeout and protocol versions from .stella/run-gateway.json mcp)
entries.outputs: {bind, port, path, pid} on stdout and at the index key capabilities_mcp_state; per request a JSON-RPC answer, or an HTTP status >= 400 with a JSON-RPC error whose data.code is the catalog code (STL-GRD-675..679); a refused tool call is a result with isError true (STL-GRD-660..667); exit 1 with STL-GRD-680 or STL-CFG-312 when it cannot serve

entries.summary: Stuck detection (host only): scan a run's trusted tool stream for no-progress patterns (same action and result repeated, same error repeated, two actions alternating, an edit followed by its revert, tokens spent with no diff change) with per-role thresholds from .stella/stuck.json; watch a run and on a match stop it (adapter stop), write one trusted run-block event line with the matching events, and block the card through the data-configured block command
entries.inputs: scan FILE [--role R] [--json] | watch --run R --card C [--role R] [--events FILE]
entries.outputs: scan: {stuck, role, matches[{pattern, detail, evidence}]}; watch: {run, blocked, pattern, reason}; exit 1 with a catalog code (STL-ESC-250..253, STL-CFG-312 worker environment)

entries.summary: The QA loop of a card (host only): round state folded from trusted qa.* event lines, open with the tier floor, raise, the owner trigger, freeze of a commit into a disposable standalone clone (hooks off) with the diff and fix triggers, the round plan (counts, depths, forced roles, Local only, slots with distinct links) and done on an exact hash
entries.inputs: open --card C --project P --tier T --base H --builder-role R [--trigger ID]... | raise --card C --tier T --reason TEXT | trigger --card C --id ID | freeze --card C --repo PATH --hash H | plan --card C --json | status --card C [--head H] --json | done --card C --hash H
entries.outputs: JSON (one line per trusted event line written; plan and status as JSON); exit 1 with a catalog code (STL-QA-100..108, STL-CFG-312 in a worker environment), and with --json {card, code, problem}; done exits 0 only when the last round passed on exactly that hash

entries.summary: Policy layer: the stack rules (write boundary, protected paths, secret reads, commit rule, dispatcher-only actions, model limits) written once in .stella/policy.json and rendered into each worker CLI's own permission config through the shapes of .stella/adapters.json; checks the data (every rule kind carried by each adapter, token variables are worker signals, writable paths only the worktree), regenerates the committed generated configs, catches a hand edit of a generated block (drift), and judges one tool call for a CLI that runs a hook.
entries.inputs: check [--json] | generate --adapter A [--worktree W] [--out F] [--json] | generate --all [--write] [--json] | drift [--json] | hook --adapter A [--worktree W] (a tool call payload on stdin)
entries.outputs: JSON (check: {ok, problems[{code, problem}]}; generate: the rendered config, or {adapter, file, pointers}; generate --all: {changed, written}; drift: {ok, drift[{adapter, file, pointers, problem, code}]}); hook: nothing (no objection) or the adapter's deny template; exit 1 with a catalog code (STL-GRD-610 data unusable, 611 a rule kind an adapter does not carry, 612 token variable not a worker signal, 613 drift, 614 writable beyond the worktree, 615-617 hook refusals, 618 unknown adapter)

entries.summary: Per-role run policy (token-lean tools, budgets, context policy): check the data, show a role's policy, translate it to an adapter's settings (unsupported features listed), compare prefill and output with the role's budget
entries.inputs: check|show|translate|prefill|output-check --role R [--adapter A] [--tokens N|--file F|--events F] --json
entries.outputs: JSON; exit 1 with STL-LIM-450..453 when the policy is unusable or a budget is exceeded

entries.summary: Deterministic log filter: trims tool output to the failing lines with context, collapses repeated lines, drops progress noise; never drops a failing line
entries.outputs: the filtered log on stdout; exit 1 with STL-LIM-450 when the policy is unusable

entries.summary: Approval-service channel adapter: delivers a request to its Discord thread and collects the owner answer
entries.inputs: a request JSON on stdin (deliver) or a collect call
entries.outputs: a message ref; answer lines

entries.summary: Approval-service channel adapter for the host terminal: shows the request and how to answer it
entries.outputs: a message ref on stdout; the request on stderr

entries.summary: Approval-service resume: unblocks the card that waited on an approval, with the decision as the reason
entries.outputs: the card unblocked

entries.summary: Write or check the generated alert code page docs/alert-codes.md from the alert catalog
entries.outputs: docs/alert-codes.md written, or exit 1 when stale

entries.summary: Print one alert code's catalog entry for the terminal
entries.inputs: an alert code such as STL-ESC-210
entries.outputs: the entry as text

entries.summary: Sourced helpers that render an owner-facing alert line from the catalog and send it to the alerts channel
entries.outputs: a plain-language line; a line in the alerts log; a channel message

entries.summary: Re-apply the repo-managed Hermes local config (soul rules, hooks, toolsets) to the Hermes volume
entries.outputs: the Hermes profiles updated

entries.summary: Simulation of Hermes's real approval gate with a stub channel
entries.outputs: a pass or fail report

entries.summary: Benchmark suite: list, check, run and measure the tasks in bench/tasks
entries.inputs: a subcommand (list, check, reset, verify, metrics, run)
entries.outputs: task ids, verdicts and metrics JSON

entries.summary: Live probe of the OS box: prints PROBE lines for attacks run boxed and unboxed
entries.outputs: PROBE lines

entries.summary: Test rig: a fake coding CLI driven by an action list in its prompt (write, read, edit, shell, MCP call, model call, env, usage); obeys its generated policy config and hook the way its adapter entry says and prints jsonl
entries.outputs: jsonl tool_use, tool_result, usage and result lines on stdout; exit 0, 1 when an action crashes

entries.summary: Conformance suite for worker adapters (host only): run each case of .stella/conformance.json as a card-less adapter run in a scratch worktree, judge it from trusted evidence (stream, run log, completion evidence, usage ledger, event log, worktree), record the result with the data digests the adapter start gate checks
entries.outputs: JSON record {adapter, version, role, link, conn_type, passed, cases, digests, at, global_id, install_id}; the record at the index key conformance_records; one conformance.run event line; exit 1 with a catalog code (STL-GRD-690..695, STL-CFG-312 worker environment)
